lines.text: KVM runs the processor and the memory. Everything else, the disk, the network card, is pretended by an ordinary program on the host: the virtual machine monitor.
The classic one, QEMU, can pretend to be a whole PC: USB, sound cards, even a floppy drive.
Each of those devices is code that a hostile guest can poke at.
In 2015, a bug in QEMU's floppy drive, called VENOM, let code in a virtual machine break out onto the host.
Almost none of those machines ever used a floppy.
Firecracker takes the opposite road. Amazon wrote it in Rust to run AWS Lambda, and open-sourced it in 2018.
It pretends a handful of devices: a disk, a network card, a console, and little else.
Less to pretend is less to attack, and less to wait for: Firecracker can start a machine's code in about 125 milliseconds, with under five megabytes of overhead.
It can also freeze a running machine to disk, and bring it back in milliseconds.
Spunto Sandbox is built on it.
